title: Central Angle From Distance Calculator
description: Convert a surface distance into Earth's central angle with the Central Angle From Distance Calculator — degrees, radians and circumference share. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, New York to London's 5,540 km of surface distance subtends 49.82° at Earth's centre — about 13.84% of the whole circumference, the angle a 'digging' line between them would make.
quick_answer: The Central Angle From Distance Calculator converts a great-circle surface distance into the angle it subtends at Earth's centre, in degrees and radians. Enter the distance and read the angle — the quantity behind satellite visibility, seismic wave paths and every through-Earth chord.

body.t: Earthquake waves are reported by epicentral angle (Δ) — degrees from source to station. Distances convert to Δ here; 90° is a quarter-planet away, wherever you stand.
Coverage cones and visibility windows start from the central angle between a ground station and the sub-satellite point.

The central angle in radians is just distance ÷ radius — the one place the radian is not a convention but a measurement.
1 km → 0.0090°. 100 km → 0.8993°. 1,000 km → 8.9932°. Each is distance ÷ 6,371.0088 km, in radians wearing degrees — the calculator's entire formula, because Earth's radius is the exchange rate.
